title: Thalys
extract:
Thalys is an Incarnon ceremonial Heavy Scythe. In its transformed state, struck enemies are embedded with a Void shard, with each new shard causing existing shards to inflict damage on their hosts.

Characteristics
This weapon deals primarily  Slash damage.
As an Incarnon weapon, Thalys has 5 evolution tiers with different perks that allow players to customize their Thalys' stats.
Once unlocked, activate Incarnon Form by executing a Heavy Attack with a Melee Combo of 6x or higher.
When the transformation is ready, the combo counter will shimmer with Void energy.
Incarnon Form lasts for 90 seconds and behaves as follows:
Attacks embed a damaging shard in enemies.

Acquisition
Thalys' blueprint is purchased from Acrithis or Dominus Thrax in the Dormizone for 96  Scuttler Husk awarded from Isleweaver in Duviri. Access requires completion of The Hex Quest.

Notes
When newly acquired from the Foundry, players must acquire 100 kills with the Thalys in order to gain access to its Incarnon transformation. Each challenge additionally grants 5,000 affinity to the weapon, affected by Affinity Boosters. The following Evolution tiers, their requirements for unlocking them, and their related perks, are shown below.

Overview
Incarnon Form is charged by building Melee Combo to 6x, then using a Heavy Attack. Once activated, the Incarnon form lasts for 90 seconds.
Incarnon Form persists through all activities, such as holstering, bleedout, or being disarmed. However, Incarnon Form is removed upon death.

Evolutions

Tips
Combining  Corrupt Charge (or more ideally  Galvanized Reflex) and Adept Reflexes grants a passive minimum 3x Melee Combo, allowing Swift Transmute to immediately transform Thalys at will.
When using a ground finisher to embed a new enemy with a shard, the 12x damage multiplier of the finisher will be applied to shard trigger damage on all previously embedded targets.

Trivia
The name Thalys may be derived from "Thal", an older spelling of German Tal, meaning "valley", and French "Lys", meaning "lily".
Thalys is also the name of a European high speed train service.
